title: Avoid npm for project tooling and prefer native established alternatives
summary: Do not invoke or recommend npm; use Cargo, Lua, existing Rust/native tools, or an approved alternative appropriate to the project.
statement: Do not use or instruct the project owner to use npm for installation, development, building, testing or release workflows. Prefer Rust/Cargo for application implementations, Lua for scripting, and existing native tools or maintained preinstalled dependencies. For Arch-based operating-system package management prefer the owner's established yay workflow rather than imposing another manager. Respect existing project toolchains and external dependencies where feasible, but if a required upstream workflow specifically depends on npm, report the concrete need and constraints and request explicit authorization for an alternative strategy; do not silently run npm, rewrite unrelated build systems, or pretend npm-dependent work was verified.
rationale: Do not invoke or recommend npm; use Cargo, Lua, existing Rust/native tools, or an approved alternative appropriate to the project. Builds on existing published Nomos constraints without rewriting historical rules.

conditions: Work involves selecting, invoking, documenting or requesting developer-facing package/build tools.
exceptions: Project-specific constraints override generic tool preferences only when explicitly authorized; never invoke npm without the owner's change of instruction.
Do not unnecessarily replace or disrupt existing project build systems outside authorized scope.
